event_data.continuation_prompt:
StoryForge Observability Mission — Cycle 3 of 3 (FINAL HARDENING)

Cycles 1 and 2 established a full observability stack for the AI-StoryForge FastAPI application at /home/vader/AI-AtlasForge/workspace/AI-StoryForge/. The test suite now has 103 passing tests across categories A–V. All implementations use stdlib only.

Cycle 3 is the final cycle. It must bring the observability layer to production-grade completeness with four remaining work items:

(1) DISTRIBUTED TRACE CONTEXT PROPAGATION (Category W, 5 tests)
The current request_id_middleware generates a UUID per request from scratch. Real microservice deployments forward W3C Trace Context headers (traceparent, tracestate). Implement:
  - Read incoming 'traceparent' header (format: 00-<trace-id>-<span-id>-<flags>) and re-use the trace-id if present, generating only a new span-id
  - If no traceparent header, generate a fresh trace-id + span-id and emit a valid traceparent header in the response
  - Store both trace_id and span_id in ContextVar alongside request_id
  - Include trace_id and span_id in every structured JSON log line and every audit record
  - Add X-Trace-ID and X-Span-ID response headers on all responses
  Tests: (a) no incoming traceparent → response has valid traceparent header; (b) incoming traceparent propagated with new span-id; (c) malformed traceparent treated as absent; (d) trace_id appears in log output; (e) span_id appears in audit record

(2) CIRCUIT BREAKER FOR EXTERNAL CALLS (Category X, 5 tests)
The webhook sender and any future external HTTP calls should be protected by a lightweight circuit breaker. Implement a stdlib CircuitBreaker class in web/circuit_breaker.py:
  - States: CLOSED (normal), OPEN (failing, reject fast), HALF_OPEN (probe)
  - Opens after N consecutive failures (STORYFORGE_CB_FAILURE_THRESHOLD, default 5)
  - Stays open for M seconds (STORYFORGE_CB_OPEN_SECONDS, default 60) before moving to HALF_OPEN
  - One probe request allowed in HALF_OPEN; success → CLOSED, failure → OPEN again
  - Thread-safe with threading.Lock
  - Integrate with the webhook sender in audit.py
  Tests: (a) circuit starts CLOSED; (b) N failures → OPEN; (c) fast-fail in OPEN state; (d) HALF_OPEN probe success → CLOSED; (e) HALF_OPEN probe failure → OPEN

(3) RATE LIMIT PER-ENDPOINT METRICS (Category Y, 4 tests)
The /metrics endpoint currently reports auth_failures_total. Extend it with per-endpoint rate limit hit counters:
  - Track rate_limit_hits_total{endpoint='/login'}, rate_limit_hits_total{endpoint='/register'}, rate_limit_hits_total{endpoint='/api/generate'} etc.
  - Increment counters from the existing rate limiter middleware in web/limiter.py whenever a 429 is returned
  - Expose in /metrics Prometheus text format as: rate_limit_hits_total{endpoint="/login"} 42
  - Also expose rate_limit_hits_total (aggregate across all endpoints)
  Tests: (a) baseline counter is 0; (b) hitting rate limit increments endpoint counter; (c) Prometheus text format has correct label syntax; (d) aggregate counter equals sum of per-endpoint counters

(4) FINAL INTEGRATION TEST AND MISSION REPORT (Category Z, 3 tests + report)
  - Write a Category Z end-to-end integration test in tests/test_security_regression.py that:
      (a) Starts the app, fires 50 mixed requests (login attempts, story generates, health checks, /metrics polls)
      (b) Asserts /metrics shows non-zero counters for total_requests, health_check_total
      (c) Asserts audit.jsonl has at least one record for each event type (LOGIN_ATTEMPT, STORY_GENERATED, HEALTH_CHECK)
  - After all tests pass, write a mission completion report to workspace/AI-StoryForge/OBSERVABILITY_REPORT.md covering:
      * Architecture overview of the observability layer (structured logging, audit trail, metrics, health checks, sampling, webhook alerts, circuit breaker, trace context)
      * All environment variables and their defaults
      * Endpoint reference (/health, /readyz, /metrics) with response schema
      * Test coverage summary (categories A–Z)

Final target: 103 + 17 new = 120 tests passing, 0 failing.
Test command: STORYFORGE_PORT=5100 python3 tests/test_security_regression.py
All implementations must use stdlib only — no new pip dependencies.
The system must pass end-to-end (not just unit-level) before marking the mission complete.

cycle_report.summary: Cycle 2 hardened and extended the StoryForge observability layer with 6 production-readiness features: configurable log sampling, a Prometheus-compatible /metrics endpoint, audit log rotation stress testing, alert webhook robustness with retry/backoff, /health degradation mode (HTTP 207), and structured JSON error responses with X-Request-ID on all error paths. All 26 new tests pass alongside the original 78, achieving 103 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped (the single skip is an optional live-runtime check that requires an external webhook receiver).
achievements: Category Q (Log Sampling, 5 tests): STORYFORGE_LOG_SAMPLE_RATE env var (0.0–1.0, default 1.0) probabilistically drops non-error request logs while always preserving errors and audit events. Validated boundary values (0.0, 1.0) and midpoint sampling distribution.

Category R (Metrics Endpoint, 5 tests): /metrics returns Prometheus text format (or JSON fallback) with counters total_requests, auth_failures_total (per-IP bucket), security_alerts_total, health_check_total, and a streaming P-value histogram (p50/p95/p99) for request_duration — all implemented in stdlib with no external dependencies.

Category S (Audit Log Rotation, 3 tests): Stress test generates 1000+ audit records and verifies file size stays bounded, backup files (audit.jsonl.1, .2, …) are created by RotatingFileHandler, and all records remain valid JSONL after rotation.

Category T (Alert Webhook Robustness, 4 tests): STORYFORGE_ALERT_WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT controls request timeout (default 5s). All network exceptions are caught so webhook failure never surfaces to request handlers. Webhook send outcome (success/failure) is logged as structured JSON. Exponential backoff retry (up to 2 retries, cap 10s) implemented. Verified with stdlib http.server mock.

Category U (Health Degradation Mode, 4 tests): /health now returns HTTP 207 Multi-Status when ≥1 check fails, with top-level status:'degraded' and per-check breakdowns. /readyz returns 503 on any failure. HTTP 200 still returned when all checks pass. Status codes documented in comment block.

Category V (Structured Error Responses, 4 tests): All exception handlers (500, 422, 429, 404) audited and standardised. Every error response is a JSON object with fields request_id, error_code, message, timestamp. X-Request-ID header present on all error responses.
Zero regressions: all original 78 tests (A–P + LIVE) continue to pass.
Total test count: 103 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (live webhook receiver optional).
issues: Category LIVE test 3 (live webhook delivery) is skipped when no external webhook receiver is available at test time — this is expected and by design; the test framework marks it as skipped rather than failed.

metrics.py StreamingHistogram uses reservoir sampling for p-value accuracy; under very high concurrency a lock-free approach would be preferable, but stdlib threading.Lock is sufficient for current load targets.
